v.rationale: All three share the same core design: onOneServer, withoutOverlapping with an expiry, a unique job whose lock is shorter than the hourly interval, and batched id deletes. Probes confirmed that a second server in the same minute does not double-dispatch, that the unique lock is released after both successful and failed runs, and that a 5,001-row batch prune works in all three. (A probe of overlap-lock expiry failed identically everywhere because the array cache lock ignores TTL in isLocked, so it is not counted.) impl-2 ranks first on test depth: real schedule:run dispatch, timezone and onOneServer assertions for every task, DST-day and boundary cases, idempotency and mail rendering, plus a tidy group() and Redis in .env.example. Its only operational nit is the foreground prune delaying the sync dispatch. impl-1 is nearly equal and arguably better on runtime details (runInBackground prune, cutoff computed once, a useful DST comment), but its tests are slightly thinner and it leaves the cache and queue defaults at database. impl-3 leaves database retry_after at 90s against a 2700s timeout, a real double-run risk on the database queue. Its schedule tests mostly assert cron strings, and it has unused imports, a filler test and less idiomatic test setup, so it ranks last.
